findings.summary: The caption calls the solved lower null 'the hollow blue cross', but the PNG renders it as a solid filled blue X (ms 9, mew 1.6, drawn by draw_nulls in the solved colour). A reader told to look for a hollow cross finds a solid one, while the only hollow mark in the figure is EFIT's ring. The sentence exists to settle which mark is which, so its wording should match what is drawn.

The caption calls EFIT's null 'the open grey ring', but the ring renders near-black (#333333), which is the darkest mark in the figure after the text; the only grey the reader can see is the first-wall trace (#929292). 'Grey' therefore points a reader at the wrong ink in a figure whose ring-versus-wall colours are what the caption is describing.

The legend labels the lower-null markers 'solved X-point' and 'EFIT X-point' on every panel, but on 146 limited and 179 limited the marks are limiter contacts low in the vessel rather than X-points. The caption carries the distinction, so a reader who reads the caption is not misled; a reader scanning the legend alone is told the mark in the limited panels is an X-point.

rubric_lines: RUBRIC legibility: passes; four poloidal panels read at a glance, and the repair round's ring-versus-cross pair is now distinguishable on all four rows. On 137 diverted and 146 diverted the near-black open ring sits around the solid blue cross at the separatrix crossing, so the achieved null is visible instead of hidden behind EFIT's marker; on 146 limited and 179 limited the ring and the cross stand apart with the dashed leader between them (179 limited: cross inside the ring's right side, ring stroke intact, both shapes legible).
RUBRIC data_ink: passes; contours, one thick clipped level, the first-wall trace and the topology markers carry all the visual weight on plain white, with three annotation lines per panel.
RUBRIC decoration: passes; axes off, no grid, frame, background fill, title or suptitle; one unframed six-entry legend row at the top, and nothing else that is not data or a panel note.
RUBRIC contrast: passes; annotation and legend text render at #0b0b0b on white, and the first-wall trace at #929292 reads as a receding reference at full size.

RUBRIC table_form: passes; the image is a spatial poloidal flux map of four terminal states, and the three numeric lines under each panel annotate that panel rather than depicting a table as an image.

RUBRIC label_collision: passes; no text label is clipped or overlapping, the rightmost note line under 179 limited ends well inside the canvas, and the legend row clears the panels. Marker-on-marker overlap on 179 limited is the intended eccentricity the caption describes, not a collision.

rubric_verdicts.contrast: All text renders at #0b0b0b on white and clears any contrast floor. The first-wall trace at #929292 is the receding reference the style rule asks for and reads acceptably at full size.
rubric_verdicts.data_ink: The data carry the weight: blue contour lines, one thicker clipped level, a grey wall trace, one triangle and one ring/cross pair per panel on white. The only non-data ink is the single legend row and the three note lines per panel.
rubric_verdicts.decoration: No decorative ink: axes off, no grid, no frame, no background fill or gridlines, no title or suptitle, and the legend is frameless.
rubric_verdicts.label_collision: No text label is clipped, overlapping another, or over the data: the panel notes sit in the figure margin below their panels and the legend row sits above them. Measured on the PNG, the rightmost note ends inside the canvas.
rubric_verdicts.legibility: The figure reads at a glance as four terminal flux states: one magnetic-axis triangle inside the closed contours of every panel, thin blue contour fans, one thick blue clipped level, a grey first-wall trace, and three lines under each panel giving the residual, the convergence flag and the lower-null offset in cm and the band in kA. The defect the previous round reported - EFIT's marker painted over the solved one, hiding the achieved null - is repaired in the render: the solved null is a solid blue cross and EFIT's is an open near-black ring, and the pair is separable on all four rows.
rubric_verdicts.table_form: The four per-panel numbers are annotations of the plotted state, not a table rendered as an image; the spatial flux map is the natural form for this data.
